\[
i^1 = i, \quad i^2 = -1, \quad i^3 = -i, \quad i^4 = 1
\]

\[
i^{11} = i, \quad i^{16} = i^2 = -1, \quad i^{21} = i^3 = -i, \quad i^{26} = i^2 = -1, \quad i^{31} = i^3 = -i
\]

\[
i + (-1) + (-i) + (-1) + i
\]

\[
(i - i) + (-1 - 1 - 1) = 0 + (-3) = -3
\]

\[
\boxed{-3}
\]

grade.gold_answer: We know that by definition, $i^2=-1$, so $i^4=(-1)^2=1.$ More generally, for all integers k, $i^{4k}=(i^4)^k=1^k=1$. Since $i^3=-i$, we can simplify this to get our final result: $i^{11} + i^{16} + i^{21} + i^{26} + i^{31}=-i+1+i-1-i=\boxed{-i}.$
